messages:
leo: FYI support ticket INC-4321 - customer on Safari 16.4 reporting SSE stream drops after ~25-40s. They see partial chunks and then reconnect loops. High token billing spike because client polyfill opens new EventSource on reconnect.

maria: thanks leo. do we have repro steps and a sample request from the customer? any headers (ETag/If-None-Match / 304) showing up?

leo: here's what the customer pasted (redacted):

curl -v \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-x\" \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \n  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream'

response snippet:
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 14:02:02 GMT
< Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
< Transfer-Encoding: chunked
< ETag: \"abcd1234\"
< Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600
< Age: 215

later (on reconnect attempt):
< GET /v1/stream?model=gpt-x HTTP/1.1
< If-None-Match: \"abcd1234\"
< HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified

customer says: when we get 304 mid-stream, browser EventSource stops with no further data; polyfill then opens new EventSource which sometimes hits authorization/ratelimit, then loops.

leo: repro steps they provided in browser:

1) open Safari 16.4 on macOS 13.5
2) create EventSource to /v1/stream with auth cookie/token
3) after ~30s, observe partial event (truncated JSON) then connection silently closes
4) polyfill reconnects immediately -> new stream -> duplicate events, partial final chunk missing

code they use (simplified):

const es = new EventSource('/v1/stream?session=abc123', { withCredentials: true });
es.onmessage = (e) => { console.log('msg', e.data); }
es.onerror = (e) => { console.warn('es err', e); es.close(); /* polyfill auto-reopen upstream */ }

olivia: thanks for the logs. two initial thoughts: 1) SSE endpoints must not be cached / return 304. 2) Safari's EventSource is sensitive to chunk boundaries and ends stream on unexpected connection semantics. the ETag/Cache-Control/public + Age from CDN suggests the CDN is returning cached responses or 304s. can we get server access logs showing request/response pairs and any intermediate CDN? also, is the customer behind a proxy that might inject If-None-Match?

ashwin: agree. we've seen proxies/CDNs coalescing SSE responses into cached 304 cycles before. key fixes: set Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate (or at least no-cache with Vary: Authorization and Vary: Origin) and ensure we never send ETag for streaming endpoints. also set Surrogate-Control: no-store for Fastly/CF. this avoids intermediate 304s and forces fresh keep-alive.

leo: customer said they cannot change their CDN rules. asking for short-term mitigation we can apply from server side.

olivia: short-term workaround we can server-side: remove ETag + set Cache-Control: private, no-transform, no-cache and add a short-lived SSE keepalive chunk every 10s with \":\n\" comment line so proxies treat it as dynamic. also add header: Vary: Authorization to prevent shared cache across different users. if proxy still returns 304 due to If-None-Match, we can switch stream endpoints to return 200 with small heartbeat body when If-None-Match present (avoid 304 semantics).

leo: can we try a quick patch on staging to force no-cache on /v1/stream? customer open to testing.

olivia: yep. I'll open a small canary deploy and route a test customer. plan: add middleware for SSE paths to strip If-None-Match from request before upstream and set response headers: Cache-Control: no-cache, Surrogate-Control: no-store, Pragma: no-cache, Vary: Authorization. also remove ETag generation.

ashwin: small note — removing ETag is fine, but some CDN configs will still return 304 if they see If-None-Match in the request regardless. we should drop the header server-side (strip incoming If-None-Match) and respond 200 with proper streaming content. that avoids forcing CDNs into 304 flow.

leo: customer asked if there's a client-side workaround in the meantime.

olivia: immediate client workaround: add a cache-busting query param to the SSE URL (e.g., ?t=Date.now()) or use WebSocket fallback. also ensure the polyfill has exponential backoff to avoid immediate reopen storms. example:

const url = `/v1/stream?session=abc123&t=${Date.now()}`;
const es = new EventSource(url);

— downside: cache-bust increases load but prevents 304s.

leo: customer requested exact repro they can run locally. olivia, can you paste the curl that simulates the If-None-Match path?

olivia: sure. to simulate the CDN returning 304 midstream you can do: 

# start an initial stream to get an ETag
curl -i -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer TOKEN' \"https://staging.redwood.example/v1/stream?session=test\" > /tmp/first.txt
# extract ETag then re-request with If-None-Match to emulate cached client
ETAG=$(grep -i ETag /tmp/first.txt | awk '{print $2}')
curl -i -H \"If-None-Match: $ETAG\" -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \"https://staging.redwood.example/v1/stream?session=test\"

that should give a 304 from a cache-enabled edge. test will show client behavior.

leo: thank you. i'll share steps with customer and try to schedule canary test later today.

deploy-bot: canary deploy created: release sse-no-cache-2026-02-12 to cluster staging-sse (sha: abcdef). patch includes middleware to strip If-None-Match and set Cache-Control headers.

ashwin: after canary, let's monitor metrics: SSE disconnect rate, reconnections per session, token usage per user to see billing spike. also check our logs for any 304 responses still being emitted from upstream or edge.

maria: good plan. leo, mark INC-4321 as \"awaiting customer test\" and add label: sse-cache-304. escalate to eng-runtime for post-mortem if canary reduces errors.

leo: done. customer will try the canary tomorrow morning and report. tagging @olivia @ashwin to follow up. :thumbsup:
